t: You're looking at the memorial to Richard Trevithick, on Gower Street. It was made by the sculptor Leonard Merrifield, who is known for public monuments in Cornwall and Northern Ireland. Trevithick was born in Cornwall's mining country, the son of a mining captain. He became an early pioneer of steam on road and rail, developed the first high-pressure steam engine, and built the first working railway steam locomotive. On 21 February 1804, his locomotive hauled a train along the Penydarren Ironworks tramway in Merthyr Tydfil, the world's first locomotive-hauled railway journey.
